objective: A documented governance body owns cybersecurity decisions, meets on a defined cadence, and its decisions are minuted and traceable.
A current, approved policy set covers every control domain in scope, with a named owner and a review interval per policy.

control_title: Roles, responsibilities and segregation of duties
objective: Security responsibilities are assigned to named roles, and conflicting duties cannot be exercised by one person.
Applicable laws, regulations and contractual security obligations are recorded, mapped to controls, and reviewed when they change.
Every deviation from a control is time-bound, justified, approved by someone other than the requester, and carries a compensating control.
All compute, storage, network and data assets in scope are discoverable in an inventory that is refreshed automatically.
Each asset carries an accountable owner and a data classification that drives its control baseline.
New or unmanaged assets appearing in the environment are detected and either enrolled or removed within a defined window.
Every human and machine actor authenticates under a unique identity; shared and generic accounts are eliminated or individually attributed.
MFA is enforced for all interactive access, without exception for administrators or remote access.
Permissions are granted at the minimum scope needed, privileged access is time-bound or brokered, and standing admin rights are the exception.
Entitlements are reviewed on a defined cadence by the accountable owner, and removals are evidenced.
Access is provisioned on hire, adjusted on role change, and revoked on exit within a defined SLA, driven by the HR system of record.
Static credentials are rotated or replaced by short-lived tokens; secrets never live in source, images or configuration files.
Data at rest is encrypted using approved algorithms, with encryption enabled by default rather than per resource.
All data in transit uses current TLS; plaintext protocols and deprecated cipher suites are refused at the endpoint.
Keys are generated, stored and rotated in a managed key service, with separation between key custodians and data owners.
Certificates are inventoried, monitored for expiry, and renewed before failure rather than after an outage.
Environments and trust zones are segmented so that a compromise in one does not grant reachability to another.
Inbound access is denied by default; every allowed path is justified, scoped and reviewed.
Outbound traffic is restricted to known destinations, which is what turns a foothold into a contained incident.
Internet-facing services sit behind rate limiting and volumetric attack protection with tested thresholds.
Data is classified, and handling rules for each class are enforced technically rather than only stated in policy.
Data subject to residency obligations is stored and processed only in permitted regions, and this is verifiable from configuration.
Backups are taken to a defined RPO, protected from the same failure domain, and restoration is tested - not assumed.
Media and cloud storage are sanitised or cryptographically erased when decommissioned, with evidence retained.
Security-relevant events are logged across all in-scope systems, including the control plane of cloud accounts.
Logs are tamper-evident, stored separately from the systems producing them, and retained for the required period.
Detections exist for defined threat scenarios, alerts route to a staffed channel, and detection gaps are tracked.
Systems synchronise to a trusted time source, without which correlated forensic reconstruction is not possible.
Authenticated scanning covers all in-scope assets on a defined cadence, and coverage gaps are treated as findings.
Vulnerabilities are remediated within severity-based deadlines, and overdue items escalate rather than age quietly.
Independent testing is performed at a defined frequency and after significant change, with findings tracked to closure.
Managed endpoints run current protective tooling that reports centrally, and unprotected endpoints are detected.
Production changes are authorised, recorded, and traceable to a request; emergency changes are reviewed retrospectively.
Systems are built from hardened baselines, and drift from those baselines is detected and corrected.
Infrastructure changes go through code review and automated policy checks before they reach production.
Continuity plans define RTO and RPO per service, name decision-makers, and are exercised at least annually.
In-scope services tolerate the loss of a single availability zone or node without breaching their stated RTO.
Recovery is tested against the documented RTO, and the test result - not the plan - is the evidence.
Third parties are inventoried and tiered by the impact of their failure or compromise.
Assurance is obtained before onboarding and refreshed on a tier-based cadence.
Contracts carry security, breach-notification and audit-rights clauses proportionate to the vendor tier.
Personal data processing has a recorded lawful basis, and consent - where relied on - is granular and withdrawable.
Access, correction, deletion and portability requests are fulfilled within the statutory deadline and evidenced.
A record of processing activities is maintained and reconciles to the actual systems holding personal data.
Transfers of personal data outside the jurisdiction are assessed, approved and technically constrained.
The organisation can detect, assess and notify a personal data breach within the statutory window.
Screening proportionate to role sensitivity is completed before access is granted.
All staff complete role-appropriate training on a defined cadence, and completion is tracked to the individual.
Staff acknowledge acceptable use and confidentiality obligations, and acknowledgements are retrievable.
A tested plan defines severity levels, roles, escalation paths and external notification obligations.
Incidents are detected, triaged against defined severity criteria, and time-stamped from detection to closure.
Significant incidents produce a documented review with corrective actions tracked to completion.
Every cloud account is enrolled under organisational guardrails before workloads are deployed into it.
Cloud configuration is continuously evaluated against a defined standard, and drift raises a finding.
Container platforms enforce least privilege, admission control and image provenance.
Storage, databases and management interfaces are prevented from becoming publicly reachable, not merely detected afterwards.
Security requirements, threat modelling and review gates are part of the delivery process rather than a pre-release checklist.
Third-party components are inventoried and scanned, and vulnerable dependencies block release above a defined severity.

control_title: Static and secret scanning in CI
objective: Code is scanned for vulnerabilities and committed secrets before merge, with findings failing the build.
Protected branches require review and passing checks; direct pushes to production branches are not possible.

control_title: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
objective: The mission of the organization is articulated and used as the lens through which cybersecurity risks are evaluated.

control_title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
objective: Stakeholders are mapped and their cybersecurity expectations are explicit inputs to the program.

control_title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity—including privacy and civil liberties obligations—are understood and managed
objective: All applicable laws, regulations, and contract clauses are tracked and traced to controls.

control_title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
objective: The services on which others depend are inventoried and protected accordingly.

control_title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
objective: The supplier ecosystem and external dependencies are mapped and risk-tiered.

control_title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
objective: Cybersecurity risk objectives are explicit, written, and signed off by leadership.

control_title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
objective: How much risk the organization is willing to bear is documented per category.

control_title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
objective: Cyber risk is integrated with enterprise risk, not siloed.

control_title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
objective: Standard risk-response playbook (mitigate / transfer / avoid / accept) is documented.

control_title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
objective: Risk information flows up, down, and across without bottlenecks.

control_title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
objective: Risks are scored consistently using a documented method.

control_title: Strategic opportunities are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
objective: Cyber risk discussions also surface opportunities, not just threats.

control_title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
objective: Top management owns cyber risk, not just the CISO.

control_title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
objective: Everyone knows their cyber responsibilities.

control_title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
objective: Cybersecurity is funded to match its declared importance.

control_title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
objective: Cyber considerations are baked into HR processes from hire to exit.

control_title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
objective: A cyber risk management policy exists, is communicated, and has teeth.

control_title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
objective: Policy stays current with the world it operates in.

control_title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
objective: The strategy is checked for results, not just adherence.

control_title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
objective: Strategy adapts to new requirements and emerging risks.

control_title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
objective: Program performance is measured and managed.

control_title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
objective: Supply chain cyber risk has its own program, not just a contract clause.

control_title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
objective: Everyone in the supply chain knows their cyber responsibilities.

control_title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
objective: Supply chain risks are part of enterprise risk, not a sidebar.

control_title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
objective: All suppliers are inventoried and tiered.

control_title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
objective: Cyber requirements appear in contracts, not just policy.

control_title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
objective: Risk is assessed before contract signing, not after.

control_title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
objective: Vendor risks are tracked across the lifecycle, not just at onboarding.

control_title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
objective: Vendors are part of your incident plan, not strangers when you call them at 3am.

control_title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
objective: Supply chain security is monitored, not assumed.

control_title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
objective: Vendor offboarding is handled with the same care as onboarding.

control_title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
objective: Every device the organization owns or operates is inventoried.

control_title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
objective: Every software product, service, and system is inventoried.

control_title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
objective: Network architecture and data flows are documented and current.

control_title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
objective: Vendor-provided services are inventoried alongside owned assets.

control_title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
objective: Asset criticality drives control rigor.

control_title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
objective: Data inventory exists per data type with owners and lifecycles.

control_title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
objective: Lifecycle management is documented and enforced.

control_title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
objective: Continuous identification and recording of vulnerabilities.

control_title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
objective: Threat intel from external sources flows into the program.

control_title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
objective: Threat catalog is current.

control_title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
objective: Risk = threat × vulnerability × impact, computed per recorded combination.

control_title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
objective: Risks are prioritized using rigorous data.

control_title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
objective: Every risk has a chosen response with a plan.

control_title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
objective: Changes and exceptions don't bypass risk discipline.

control_title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
objective: External vulnerability disclosures are handled, not ignored.

control_title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
objective: Counterfeit and tampered hardware/software are detected before deployment.

control_title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
objective: Pre-acquisition supplier risk review is mandatory.
Self-assessment identifies improvement opportunities.

control_title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
objective: Tests and exercises drive concrete improvements.

control_title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
objective: Day-to-day operations surface improvement ideas.

control_title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
objective: Plans are living documents, not shelfware.

control_title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Identity lifecycle is owned and managed.

control_title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Identity assurance matches the risk of the interaction.

control_title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Every authenticated session uses verified credentials.

control_title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Identity tokens are protected end-to-end.

control_title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Access is least-privilege and reviewed.

control_title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
subdomain_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
objective: Physical access matches digital access in rigor.

control_title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
objective: Every employee gets cyber awareness training.

control_title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
objective: Specialized roles get role-specific training.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
objective: Stored data is encrypted, integrity-verified, and available.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
objective: Data on the wire is encrypted and integrity-protected.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
objective: Data being processed in memory and applications is protected.

control_title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
objective: Backups exist, are protected, and are restorable.

control_title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
objective: Configurations are managed, baselined, and drift-monitored.

control_title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
objective: Software lifecycle is risk-driven, not 'install and forget'.

control_title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
objective: Hardware lifecycle is risk-driven and secure-by-default.

control_title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
objective: Critical logs flow to SIEM in real time.

control_title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
objective: Only authorized software runs on managed endpoints.

control_title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
objective: Security is built into the SDLC.

control_title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
objective: Network access is controlled.

control_title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
objective: Physical environment threats are mitigated.

control_title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
objective: Systems stay up under stress.

control_title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
objective: Capacity is forecast and provisioned ahead of need.

control_title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
objective: Network behavior is monitored for anomalies.

control_title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events
objective: Physical environment is continuously watched.

control_title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
objective: Insider risk indicators are detected.

control_title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
objective: Vendor activity in the environment is logged and reviewed.

control_title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
objective: Endpoints, workloads, and data behaviors are monitored.

control_title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
objective: Alert triage moves from raw signal to characterized event.

control_title: Information is correlated from multiple sources
objective: Cross-source correlation enriches detections.

control_title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
objective: Impact assessment for each event before response is sized.

control_title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
objective: Right people get right info at right time.

control_title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
objective: Context elevates raw alerts into informed conclusions.

control_title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
objective: Crossing the criteria triggers the formal IR machinery.

control_title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
objective: When the bell rings, the plan runs.

control_title: Incident reports are triaged and validated
objective: Reported incidents are quickly assessed for accuracy and severity.
Categorization drives response.

control_title: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
objective: Right people involved at right time.

control_title: Incident response criteria are applied to determine which incidents have been resolved and to inform additional response activities
objective: Closure is data-driven, not assumed.

control_title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
objective: Root cause is found, not papered over.

control_title: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
objective: Evidence chain is preserved for legal/forensic use.

control_title: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
objective: Incident artifacts are reliably retained.

control_title: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
objective: Incident size is quantified, not guessed.

control_title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
objective: Stakeholder communication is timely and accurate.

control_title: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
objective: Information sharing reaches the right audiences with the right detail.
Containment limits damage spread.
Threat is removed from the environment.

control_title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
objective: Recovery follows the plan, not improvisation.

control_title: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
objective: Recovery is sequenced for maximum business value.

control_title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
objective: Restored data is verified clean before deployment.

control_title: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
objective: Post-incident state is sustainable, not fragile.

control_title: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
objective: Recovery is confirmed complete via objective tests.

control_title: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
objective: Recovery has a definitive end-state.

control_title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
objective: Recovery progress is transparent to stakeholders.

control_title: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging
objective: Public communications are coordinated and brand-safe.
Establish the definitions used throughout the law: personal data, sensitive personal data, processing, controller, processor, data subject, etc.
Defines when the law applies: any processing of personal data of individuals in KSA, by any controller or processor inside or outside the Kingdom.

control_title: General principles for personal data processing
objective: Mandates lawfulness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality.
Establishes the rights of data subjects: be informed, access, rectification, erasure, withhold consent, complain to the Competent Authority.
Data subjects must be informed about the processing of their data: identity of controller, purposes, lawful basis, retention, recipients, rights, transfers.
Processing requires consent OR another lawful basis recognized by the law (legal obligation, contract, vital interest, public interest, legitimate interest where balancing favors processing).
Sensitive data (race, ethnic origin, religion, beliefs, political opinion, health, biometric, genetic, criminal record) requires additional safeguards and explicit consent.
Processing of personal data of minors requires consent from a guardian and additional protective measures.
Where consent is the basis, it must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and revocable. Bundled consent is invalid.
Direct marketing using personal data requires the data subject's explicit prior consent and an easy opt-out at any time.
Personal data must be accurate and complete. Data subjects may request correction.
Data subjects can request deletion when consent is withdrawn, the purpose is served, or processing is unlawful.
Where mandated, organizations must appoint a Data Protection Officer with clear independence and authority.
DPIAs are required for high-risk processing activities, especially those involving sensitive data or large-scale monitoring.
Controllers must maintain a Record of Processing Activities documenting all personal data processing.
Appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data based on the nature, scope and context of processing.
Notify the Competent Authority and affected data subjects when a breach is likely to result in harm to individuals.
Transfer of personal data outside KSA is subject to specific conditions and safeguards. Subject to the separate Cross-Border Transfer Regulation.
Processors act only on documented instructions from the Controller. The relationship must be governed by a contract that includes specific safeguards.
Specifies the minimum content of privacy notices.
Specifies how valid consent must be obtained, recorded, and withdrawn.
Specifies the procedure for responding to data subject requests, including identity verification, scope assessment, and response timeline.

control_title: Implementing Regulation: DPIA threshold and content
objective: Specifies which processing activities require a DPIA and what the assessment must cover.
Specifies what constitutes a notifiable breach, the 72-hour notification window, content of notifications, and when to notify affected individuals.

control_title: Implementing Regulation: DPO appointment criteria and duties
objective: Specifies when DPO appointment is mandatory and what duties must be assigned to the DPO.

control_title: Cross-Border Transfer Regulation: Scope and lawful bases
objective: Defines the scope of cross-border transfer rules and the lawful bases under which such transfers may occur.

control_title: Cross-Border Transfer Regulation: Risk assessment for transfers
objective: Mandates a risk assessment for cross-border transfers covering legal, security, and operational risks.

control_title: NDMO: Personal data inventory and classification
objective: NDMO guidance on building a structured data inventory and classifying data sets by sensitivity for PDPL purposes.

control_title: NDMO: Privacy by design and default
objective: NDMO guidance to embed privacy considerations throughout system design and default settings, before deployment.
NDMO guidance on staff awareness and training programs for PDPL compliance.
NDMO guidance on continuous compliance monitoring and periodic audits.

control_title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
objective: The six core principles: lawfulness/fairness/transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. Plus accountability — controller must be able to demonstrate compliance.
Six lawful bases for processing: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests.
Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable, and easily withdrawable.

control_title: Conditions applicable to child's consent (information society services)
objective: Children below 16 (or lower per Member State, minimum 13) require parental consent for online services.

control_title: Processing of special categories of personal data
objective: Special categories (race, ethnicity, political views, religion, union membership, genetics, biometrics, health, sex life, sexual orientation) require explicit consent or one of nine specific exceptions.

control_title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions
objective: Criminal-conviction data only processed under official authority or specific Member State law.

control_title: Transparent information and modalities for exercise of rights
objective: Information must be concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible, in plain language, especially for children. Free of charge except for manifestly unfounded/excessive requests.

control_title: Information to be provided where data collected from data subject
objective: At point of collection, must provide identity/contact of controller and DPO, purposes, lawful basis, recipients, transfers, retention period, rights, complaints info.

control_title: Information to be provided where data not obtained from data subject
objective: When data is obtained from third parties, controller must inform the data subject within 1 month, or at first communication, with similar info as Art-13 plus categories of data and source.

control_title: Right of access by the data subject
objective: Data subject can request confirmation of processing and a copy of the data, plus information about purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, source, and automated decision-making.
Data subject can request correction of inaccurate or completion of incomplete data.

control_title: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
objective: Data subject can request deletion in specific circumstances (no longer needed, withdrawal of consent, objection, unlawful processing, legal obligation, child's data).
Data subject can demand temporary suspension of processing (e.g., during accuracy disputes or pending legitimate-interests assessment).

control_title: Notification obligation regarding rectification, erasure, restriction
objective: Controller must notify each recipient of data when rectification, erasure, or restriction occurs, unless impossible or disproportionate.
Where processing is by automated means based on consent or contract, data subject can receive their data in a structured, machine-readable format and transmit to another controller.
Data subject can object to processing under legitimate interests, public task, or for direct marketing. Direct marketing objection is absolute.
Data subject has right not to be subject to solely automated decisions producing legal/significant effects, with limited exceptions (contract, EU/Member State law, explicit consent).
Controller must implement technical and organizational measures to ensure and demonstrate compliance, considering nature/scope/context/purposes of processing and risks.

control_title: Data protection by design and by default
objective: Privacy must be built into system design and default configuration must be the most privacy-protective.
Where two or more controllers jointly determine purposes/means, they must determine respective responsibilities by arrangement and make essence available to data subjects.

control_title: Representatives of controllers/processors not established in the EU
objective: Non-EU controllers/processors offering goods/services to EU subjects or monitoring EU subjects must designate an EU representative.

Controllers must use only processors providing sufficient guarantees. Data Processing Agreement (DPA) must cover specific subjects (subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, types of data, categories of subjects, rights/obligations of controller).
Controllers and processors (>250 employees, or with high-risk/special-category processing) must maintain records of processing activities (RoPA) including specific information.
Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures: pseudonymisation/encryption, ongoing CIA, restoration after incidents, regular testing.

control_title: Notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority
objective: Controller must notify SA within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach (unless unlikely to result in risk). Processor must notify controller without undue delay.

control_title: Communication of personal data breach to data subject
objective: Where breach likely to result in high risk to data subjects, communicate to them without undue delay. Exceptions: encryption rendering data unintelligible; subsequent measures eliminating high risk; disproportionate effort.
DPIA required where processing likely to result in high risk: systematic profiling, large-scale special-category, large-scale public monitoring, others per SA list.

control_title: Prior consultation with the supervisory authority
objective: Where DPIA indicates high residual risk after mitigations, controller must consult SA before processing.

control_title: Designation of the data protection officer (DPO)
objective: DPO mandatory for: public authorities, large-scale systematic monitoring, or large-scale special-category/criminal-data processing.
DPO must be involved in all data-protection issues, given resources, report to highest management, no instructions on tasks, no dismissal/penalty for performing tasks.
Inform/advise organization, monitor compliance, provide DPIA advice, cooperate with SA, act as SA contact.
Transfer outside EU/EEA only if conditions in Art-45-49 met.

control_title: Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision
objective: Transfers permitted to countries with EU adequacy decision (e.g., UK, Switzerland, Canada-private-sector).
Where no adequacy, use SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses), BCRs (Binding Corporate Rules), approved codes of conduct, or approved certification.
Limited exceptions: explicit consent, contract necessity, important reasons of public interest, legal claims, vital interests, public-register data.

control_title: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
objective: Data subjects can complain to SA in their habitual residence, place of work, or alleged infringement.
Anyone suffering material/non-material damage from infringement has right to compensation.

control_title: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
objective: Tiered fines: up to €10M or 2% global turnover, or €20M or 4% global turnover for serious violations.
Specific fields a controller's RoPA must capture.
Specific fields a processor's RoPA must capture.
Information should be in clear, plain language; identifying purposes must be specific, explicit and legitimate.
Further processing for new purpose only where compatible; consider link to original purpose, context, nature of data, consequences, safeguards.
Profiling carries specific risks; subjects should have right to obtain human intervention, express their view, and contest decisions.
